body.x: Spaid (CEO Yi Chong Kul) announced its participation in CES 2025 in Las Vegas from January 7 to 10. The company aims to redefine geospatial technology by integrating live data and bridging physical and digital environments, enabling maximum information utility.

Spaid provides geospatial AI solutions that combine data from public and private entities to generate actionable insights. These solutions enable synergetic decision-making in diverse sectors, including smart city and factory digital twin operations, defense simulations, real estate site analysis, building energy control, financial risk management, and telecommunications resource management.

At CES 2025, Spaid will showcase its CES Innovation Award-winning solution, ‘AI2RE: Image to 3D Geospatial AI Metaverse,’ and preview its upcoming OpenAI-powered geospatial information platform, which will be released in early 2025.

AI2RE uses a proprietary AI engine to extract 2D vector lines from aerial imagery (satellites, drones, etc.) and generate 3D models from terrains, buildings, and roads. By automating over 80% of the conventional process, AI2RE resolves common challenges like data loss and compatibility issues, providing reliable and efficient 3D geospatial data for governments and enterprises. Its application has enhanced EU data management projects and is currently under discussion with South American and African nations.

Spaid’s OpenAI-powered platform allows users to access personalized geospatial data cards via OpenAI agents. Users can drag and drop these cards into a 3D map viewer for seamless visualization and analysis without additional tools or software. This platform aligns with Spaid’s roadmap to digitize the globe into an industrially viable metaverse through geospatial data integration.

Spaid’s CES booth visitors can experience live demonstrations of the AI2RE solution and the OpenAI-powered platform. With AI2RE, they can witness the automated process of object recognition, 2D line extraction, and 3D modeling, while the OpenAI platform will feature interactive geospatial data visualization for San Francisco.

Yi Chong Kul, CEO of Spaid, said, “Receiving the CES Innovation Award validates our ‘one-of-a-kind’ vision and the originality of our solutions. At CES 2025, we will showcase cutting-edge geospatial AI and metaverse technologies to accelerate our entry into the global market.”

AVING News, which has covered CES for 19 consecutive years, continues to bridge the gap for Korean SMEs and startups looking to expand globally. To promote Korean startups worldwide, AVING will host its Broadcasting Zone at the Venetian Expo, featuring the CES Media Day Startup Conference and global media interviews. AVING’s international media partners will cover these programs.
Following CES 2025, AVING will co-host review conferences with participating companies in Korea, offering a platform for increased visibility and improved corporate image.
